_comment: Tile manifest: the single source of truth for every Evidence Board Tile, in demo order. Tables and chart queries may only touch staging, features or ml (board/manifest.py rejects anything else); 'tables' gate readiness, and an optional chart 'reads' lists extra working tables the chart query may read without gating readiness. 2C and 2D use the deferred readiness rule, and their chart queries and 'proves' lines are placeholders, until their ticket (#96) defines them. 'proves' placeholders are filled from the chart's last row. Event matchers map recorded hook events (bin/event_recorder.py) to a Tile's activity: 'lane' (one lane per label), 'blocked' (a guardrail deny), 'approval' (a written file awaiting approval), 'timer' (started by a pre event, stopped by a failed post or a deny), 'review' (a reviewer dispatched) or 'ticker' (one entry per matching pre event, newest last); every kind but 'blocked' needs a label. 'tool' must match the whole tool name and 'summary' is searched.

tiles.title: The Northeast Spike

query: DATE_ADD(DATE_TRUNC(feed_date, WEEK(SUNDAY)), INTERVAL 6 DAY) AS week_end,
AND feed_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-06' AND DATE '2026-10-31'

tiles.proves: Northeast flu-positive counts rose {wow_pct:+.0f}% in the week ending on the Cutoff, in raw counts: the Spike the agents must explain.
tiles.proves_fallback: Northeast flu-positive counts jumped in the week ending on the Cutoff, in raw counts: the Spike the agents must explain.

tiles.title: Where the Spike lives

query: SELECT hospital_id, week_end, positive_flu_tests, positivity, share_of_ne_spike_pct
-- A Spike hospital carries at least half of an even share of the Spike.
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY ne.hospital_id ORDER BY ne.week_end)
ORDER BY ne.share_of_ne_spike_pct DESC, ne.hospital_id, ne.week_end

tiles.proves: {spike_hospitals} of {ne_hospitals} Northeast hospitals carry {spike_share_pct:.0f}% of the Spike in the week ending on the Cutoff; the other {other_hospitals} share the rest.
tiles.proves_fallback: The Spike is concentrated in specific Northeast hospitals in the week ending on the Cutoff, not spread evenly across the region.

tiles.title: Attribution of the Spike
tiles.proves: The four causes add up to the {spike_points:+.0f}% Spike; only {real_points:.0f} of those points are real disease (Outbreak plus Seasonal Ramp), the rest is the Pipeline Defect and the Sampling Artifact.
tiles.proves_fallback: Four causes (Pipeline Defect, Sampling Artifact, Outbreak and Seasonal Ramp) add up to the Spike, and only the Outbreak and Seasonal Ramp are real disease.

tiles.title: The Pipeline Defect removed

query: SELECT hospital_id, feed_date, COUNT(*) AS n
SELECT hospital_id, feed_date, COUNT(*) AS n
SELECT SUM(n) AS before_rows, COUNTIF(n > 1) AS before_duplicate_keys FROM before_keys
SELECT SUM(n) AS after_rows, COUNTIF(n > 1) AS after_duplicate_keys FROM after_keys

tiles.proves: Deduplicating by hospital and feed date removes {rows_removed:,} Hospital Feed rows across {before_duplicate_keys:,} duplicate keys, leaving {after_duplicate_keys:,} duplicate keys in staging.hospital_flu_clean.
tiles.proves_fallback: Deduplicating the Hospital Feeds by hospital and feed date removes the duplicate rows behind the Pipeline Defect.

tiles.title: Hospital Cohorts

query: SELECT cohort_id, COUNT(*) AS cohort_size, AVG(seasonal_trend) AS mean_trend
-- The Outbreak Cohort: the steepest seasonal rise, found from the data.
SELECT cohort_id AS breakout_cohort, cohort_size AS breakout_size
ORDER BY mean_trend DESC, cohort_size, cohort_id
SELECT STRING_AGG(h.hospital_id, ', ' ORDER BY h.hospital_id) AS breakout_hospitals
JOIN breakout AS b ON h.cohort_id = b.breakout_cohort
SELECT COUNT(*) AS hospitals, COUNT(DISTINCT cohort_id) AS cohorts
JOIN cohorts AS c ON h.cohort_id = c.cohort_id

tiles.proves: K-means sorts {hospitals} hospitals into {cohorts} Cohorts by seasonal shape; the steepest-rising Cohort, {breakout_cohort}, holds just {breakout_size} hospitals ({breakout_hospitals}), isolating the Outbreak in its own Cohort.
tiles.proves_fallback: K-means groups hospitals into Cohorts by seasonal shape, and the steepest-rising Cohort isolates the Outbreak hospitals.

tiles.title: WAPE leaderboard

query: -- One cell per Cohort, family and training data, averaged over periods.
ON c.cohort_id = u.cohort_id AND c.model_family = u.model_family

tiles.proves: Forecasts trained on clean data beat uncleaned data in {clean_wins} of {comparisons} Cohort and model pairs, with mean WAPE {clean_wape:.1f}% vs {uncleaned_wape:.1f}%; {best_family} leads on clean data.
tiles.proves_fallback: Forecasts trained on clean data beat forecasts trained on uncleaned data on WAPE, for both ARIMA_PLUS and TimesFM.

tiles.title: The Reveal
tiles.proves: Against the six withheld weeks after the Cutoff, the clean-data forecast tracks the truth more closely.

tiles.title: Next-period refresh
tiles.proves: The team skill reruns the whole forecasting workflow for the next epidemiological period.
